title: How to Keep a Crawl Space Dry
h1: How Do You Keep a Crawl Space Dry and Free of Moisture?
description: A damp crawl space can lead to musty smells, mold and pests. Learn where the moisture comes from and the practical steps that keep a crawl space dry.
quick_answer: Fix the water sources first: direct rain gutters and downspouts away from the house, slope soil away from the foundation, and repair plumbing leaks. Then lay a vapor barrier over the dirt floor, keep vents clear, and seal gaps where pests and damp air get in. If humidity stays high, a crawl space dehumidifier can help.
body:
Crawl spaces aren't as common here as slab foundations, but plenty of older homes in San Diego and Orange County have them. When a crawl space stays damp, the moisture works its way up into the house as musty smells, mold and pests.

What are the signs of a damp crawl space?

  • A musty smell inside the house, especially in rooms closest to the floor
  • Standing water or wet soil after rain
  • Condensation on pipes or ductwork
  • Mold or white fuzzy growth on wood joists
  • Sagging, wet or fallen insulation
  • More insects or rodents than usual
  • Floors that feel soft or cupped hardwood

Where does crawl space moisture come from?

There are usually two sources. The first is liquid water: rain running toward the foundation, downspouts dumping next to the house, irrigation spraying the walls, or a leaking pipe. The second is water vapor: moisture rising from bare soil and damp coastal air drifting in through the vents.

Most crawl spaces have some of both. The fix starts outside.

How do you stop water from getting in?

  1. Check gutters and downspouts. Clean them before the rainy season and extend downspouts several feet away from the foundation.
  2. Grade the soil. Soil and planters next to the house should slope away from it, not toward it.
  3. Adjust sprinklers so they don't spray the foundation or vents.
  4. Fix plumbing leaks under the house. A slow drip can soak the soil for months before anyone notices.
  5. Look at drainage. If water pools in the crawl space during heavy rain, a drainage solution may be needed.

How do you control moisture inside the crawl space?

Once liquid water is under control, deal with the vapor:

  • Lay a vapor barrier. A heavy plastic sheet over the dirt floor, overlapped at the seams and run a little way up the walls, blocks moisture rising from the soil.
  • Keep foundation vents clear. Many crawl spaces here are vented. Clear plants and debris so air can move.
  • Seal ductwork. Leaky ducts in a crawl space can pull damp air into the house or push cold air that causes condensation.
  • Insulate pipes and ducts that sweat.
  • Consider a dehumidifier. For crawl spaces that stay damp after these steps, a dehumidifier designed for crawl spaces can hold humidity down.

Some homes go further and fully encapsulate the crawl space, sealing the vents and walls and conditioning the space. That's a bigger project that needs careful planning, and it isn't the right fit for every home.

What about damaged insulation and pests?

Wet insulation between floor joists sags, falls and holds moisture against the wood. It should be removed and replaced once the space is dry. Rodents also like damp crawl spaces, and their droppings and nests need to be cleaned out and sanitized before new insulation goes in.

Our attic and crawl space team handles inspection, cleanup, rodent proofing, vapor barriers and new insulation. If moisture is also affecting your indoor air, our indoor air quality services can help with dehumidification and filtration upstairs.

How often should you check your crawl space?

Take a look at least once a year and after any big storm. Bring a flashlight and look for standing water, wet insulation, fresh droppings and any new smells. Catching moisture early is much easier than repairing rotted wood later.

Keep the access hatch closed and sealed, too. An open or broken hatch lets in animals and outdoor air, and it's often where problems start. If the crawl space holds your furnace or ductwork, ask for a look under the house during your yearly HVAC maintenance. A technician will already be checking duct connections and insulation, and spotting moisture at the same time saves a separate trip.

If you're buying an older home with a crawl space, add it to your inspection list. A damp crawl space is much easier to plan for before you move in than after the first rainy season.
faqs: Should crawl space vents be open or closed?

It depends on how the crawl space is built. Traditional vented crawl spaces need vents open and clear. A fully encapsulated crawl space is designed with vents sealed. Don't close vents on a standard crawl space without a plan for controlling moisture.
Is a vapor barrier worth it in Southern California?
For most crawl spaces with bare dirt floors, yes. It blocks moisture rising from the ground, which is one of the main sources of dampness even in a dry climate.
Can a damp crawl space affect the air in my home?
Yes. Air from a crawl space moves up into the house through gaps in the floor and leaky ducts, carrying musty odors, mold spores and moisture with it.
Do I need a dehumidifier in my crawl space?
Only if humidity stays high after you've fixed drainage, leaks and the vapor barrier. Many crawl spaces dry out once the water sources are handled.
